title: CLO 2025.1 - Materials & Rendering
description: CLO 2025.1 new version fully upgraded to further enhance your work efficiency! The new version also includes optimizations in material and rendering-related features. Watch the video to learn all the updates.
transcript:
This video introduces the materials and related updates to the rendering.  
Through our new storage function, you can now save the selected version and material as a clothing file in ZPLC format for storage, rather than saving the entire project.  
Choose the version to be saved in the 2D window.  
Find the storage option in the file menu.  
Click on the clothing, select it,  
enter the file name, and click Save.  
Repeat the above steps to save the hat version.  
You can see that the clothing file just saved has been stored separately.  
I will show you how to save and store the clothing.  
Previously, users had to manually delete unnecessary elements before storing.  
Now you can save only the necessary parts to simplify the workflow,  
and it does not interrupt the processing of the complete file.  
This is especially convenient when making reusable assets,  
as it is easier to use when versions and clothing assets are stored separately.  
This improves project efficiency.  
Now the hard drive in the new version can be leaked.  
This update makes the surfaces of all printed fabrics look more harmonious and can present more accurate lighting and shadow effects after rendering.  
Select the fabric and click Add Print.  
Now we can see that by default, the fabric pattern and the print pattern use two different types of decals.  
If you want to use the same decal pattern for both the fabric and the print,  
you can select the same pattern as the fabric pattern in the attribute editor.  
This function also applies to transparent materials,  
and you can select the same pattern for both the fabric and print in the attribute editor.  
The fabric pattern and the print fabric use the same PBR decal pattern.  
This allows you to present all design elements with unified lighting and texture effects.  
This is an ideal choice for designers who pursue high precision and detail.  
In the previous hollow version,  
the contrast ratio between the print fabric and the printed fabric caused some visual errors.  
In the new version,  
the hollow settings have improved accurate control over key print parameters,  
and the print fabric now clearly presents the print effect,  
which significantly improves readability and accuracy.  
Activate Print Cloth Render.  
You will see an additional information prompt next to the print fabric.  
Zoom in to check the details of the print fabric.  
Navigate to the attribute editor of the print fabric.  
First, use the double-needle print fabric as an example.  
You will see an additional part-time model ratio below.  
Activate it.  
Set the following print fabric parameters to adjust the effect of the original print fabric pattern percentage.  
Length:  
Adjust the length of the needle.  
Assign the position of the thumb and right finger of the pin.  
Penetration:  
Set the penetration pressure.  
The measured frequency of the needle is set to the minimum at the bottom in the allotment pattern.  
You will see changes in the settings.  
Adjust the distance between the name line and the edge of the applied line.  
Control the visual thickness of the real line.  
Set the width of the name line.  
Note that this parameter is more suitable for name lines with width,  
such as the edge on the left-hand side and so on.  
I will switch to the name line of the applied line here to demonstrate.  
Adjust the distance between the name line and the edge of the applied line.  
Set multiple name lines.  
Change back to the double-edged name line display.  
All changes are only visible when the model image rendering is active  
and will not affect the parameters of the actual name line itself.  
After closing the model image rendering,  
all content will return to the normal view.  
In the previous version,  
when opening the self-defined viewing pin image,  
you could only output the self-defined viewing pin image of each color,  
and could not pin the color of a specific viewing angle.  
In version 2025.1, you can choose the self-defined viewing  
based on the color of the desired viewing pin image.  
Open the rendering window.  
In the image attribute settings,  
change the viewing period to self-defined viewing.  
At this time, the color is current.  
You will see the following storage settings.  
In the settings,  
there will be a selection for the self-defined viewing pin image.  
Open the selection to render,  
which will output the color of the flag  
and the pin image under the self-defined viewing.  
This is the same as before.  
Or keep the viewing setting as self-defined viewing,  
change the color of the flag from the current flag to the full flag.  
You can also click on the self-defined color you want to choose on the right side.  
When you choose more than one flag,  
there will be a flag pin image option at the bottom,  
and an added option to select the self-defined viewing angle.  
This also means  
that in addition to the self-defined viewing pin images of each flag,  
you can also combine the flag rendering image with a selected viewing angle.  
For example, I chose viewing angle 5 here.  
After completing the settings, click on the final rendering image.  
You will get the self-defined viewing angle pin image of each flag  
and the color pin image under the selected viewing angle.  
With this update,  
users can more freely combine the color rendering images of self-defined viewing angles  
to increase work efficiency.

chunks.content: # CLO 2025.1 - Materials & Rendering This document details the material and rendering updates introduced in CLO 2025.1, focusing on new storage features, improved fabric printing, and enhanced rendering controls for self-defined viewing angles. It covers procedures, technical parameters, and improvements for designers aiming for precision in material presentation and workflow efficiency. --- ## New Clothing File Storage in ZPLC Format This section explains the new storage function that allows saving selected clothing versions and materials as separate ZPLC files, improving workflow efficiency by avoiding the need to save entire projects. - Users can now save a selected version and material as a clothing file in ZPLC format through the File menu's storage option. - The process involves selecting the clothing in the 2D window, entering a file name, and clicking Save. - Multiple clothing versions, such as hats or garments, can be saved separately using the same steps. - This feature simplifies asset management by storing only necessary parts, eliminating the previous need to manually delete unnecessary elements before saving. - Separating versions and clothing assets enhances reusability and project organization without interrupting complete file processing. --- ## Improved Fabric Printing and Surface Rendering This section covers updates to fabric printing visuals, including harmonized surface rendering, unified decal patterns, and enhanced print fabric controls for more accurate lighting, shadows, and texture effects. - The new rendering update improves the appearance of all printed fabrics, making surfaces look more harmonious with accurate lighting and shadow effects. - When adding a print to a fabric, by default, the fabric pattern and print pattern use two different decal types. - Users can now select the same PBR decal pattern for both fabric and print in the attribute editor, including transparent materials, ensuring unified lighting and texture. - This unification supports high-precision design presentation, eliminating previous contrast ratio issues that caused visual errors between print fabric and printed fabric. - The hollow settings have been enhanced for better control over print parameters, improving readability and accuracy of print effects. --- ## Print Cloth Render and Parameter Adjustments This section details the Print Cloth Render feature and how to fine-tune print fabric parameters to control stitch effects and visual details. - Activating Print Cloth Render displays an information prompt next to the print fabric in the rendering view. - In the attribute editor, parameters for print fabric, such as double-needle print fabric, include a part-time model ratio toggle to adjust the original print fabric pattern percentage. - Key parameters include: - **Length:** Adjusts the needle length. - **Penetration:** Controls needle penetration pressure. - **Frequency:** Sets the minimum needle frequency in the allotment pattern. - **Distance:** Adjusts spacing between the name line and edge of applied lines. - **Thickness:** Controls the visual thickness of real stitching lines. - **Width:** Sets the width of the name line, suitable for name lines with width such as edges.

chunks.title: CLO 2025.1 - Materials & Rendering
chunks.content: - In the attribute editor, parameters for print fabric, such as double-needle print fabric, include a part-time model ratio toggle to adjust the original print fabric pattern percentage. - Key parameters include: - **Length:** Adjusts the needle length. - **Penetration:** Controls needle penetration pressure. - **Frequency:** Sets the minimum needle frequency in the allotment pattern. - **Distance:** Adjusts spacing between the name line and edge of applied lines. - **Thickness:** Controls the visual thickness of real stitching lines. - **Width:** Sets the width of the name line, suitable for name lines with width such as edges. - Changes are visually applied only when model image rendering is active and do not modify the actual name line parameters. - Closing model image rendering returns the view to normal without permanent changes. --- ## Enhanced Self-Defined Viewing Pin Image Rendering This section explains new flexibility in rendering self-defined viewing pin images by color and viewing angle, allowing users to combine flag colors with specific angles for more efficient and customizable outputs. - Previously, users could only output self-defined viewing pin images by color but could not pin colors to specific viewing angles. - In CLO 2025.1, users can select self-defined viewing pin images based on the color of the desired viewing pin image. - To use this feature: - Open the rendering window and set the image attribute’s viewing period to self-defined viewing. - Storage settings now include a selection for self-defined viewing pin images. - Users can render output colors of flags and pin images under self-defined viewing as before. - Alternatively, keep self-defined viewing, change the flag color selection from current to full flag, and pick multiple self-defined colors. - When multiple flags are chosen, a "flag pin image" option appears with an added selection for the self-defined viewing angle. - This enables combining flag rendering images with selected viewing angles, e.g., viewing angle 5. - The final rendering produces both the self-defined viewing angle pin image of each flag and the color pin image under the selected viewing angle. - This update increases work efficiency by allowing flexible combinations of color rendering images across viewing angles. --- # Summary CLO 2025.1 introduces significant enhancements in material storage, fabric printing, and rendering workflows. The new ZPLC clothing file storage simplifies asset management by saving only selected versions and materials. Fabric printing benefits from unified PBR decal patterns and improved hollow settings, resulting in more accurate and visually consistent renderings. Advanced Print Cloth Render parameters allow detailed control over stitching effects. Finally, the rendering of self-defined viewing pin images now supports flexible color and angle combinations, enhancing customization and efficiency for designers.
